Because the cancellation fell inside the 3-minute free window, no cancellation fee is chargeable at all; the $5.00 fee on record must be refunded in full.

No-show is not a live ground for the charge on this record: the driver sent 0 in-app messages and made 0 in-app calls before the rider cancelled at 09:03:09, so NS-1(iii) cannot be met and the no-show gate in NS-1 fails even on the driver's own account.

Even if a no-show analysis applied, the 5-minute free wait never elapsed: the driver was first within 200 m of the pickup at 09:02:40 and the rider cancelled at 09:03:09, only 29 s later (platform-recorded arrival 09:02:40, cancellation 29 s after arrival).

The driver's written statement that he 'waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice' and that the rider never came down is a statement contradicted by the system records: the calls in the log are at 09:06 and 09:07, after the 09:03:09 cancellation, and no arrival/wait before 09:02:40 is recorded.
There is no in-app chat at all between rider and driver, so no message exists to evidence that the driver attempted to contact the rider in-app before cancelling, as NS-1(iii) requires.

The rider's complaint is a candid account of being delayed upstairs and giving up; it contains no threat, harassment, dangerous-driving or safety allegation, so there is no basis to divert this case to human review on safety grounds.

The rider's profile shows 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (route: 0, no-show: 0) on a 300-day-old account with a 4.5 rating, so there is no repeat no-show history under NS-9 and no basis to flag the rider's account.

The driver's clean record (4.4 years, 700 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes) is noted, but his statement that he waited over 6 minutes is inconsistent with the GPS and timeline (F2/F5/F10/F11), and missing or contradicted records favour neither party rather than the charge.
The fee is a fixed $5.00 with no surge component (multiplier 1.0×), so the disputed amount is exactly $5.00 and is refundable to the original payment method.

weaknesses: The rider admits in the complaint that she was held up and 'gave up', and the in-app reason for the cancellation is rider_changed_plans (F3) — the other side will argue this shows the cancellation was the rider's own choice, though NS-4 makes the rider's reason irrelevant inside the 3-minute window.

The driver's statement claims he waited more than 6 minutes and called twice (F12), and the driver has a long clean record with 700 trips and no disputes (F17), which the other side will use on credibility even though the call log (F10, F11) shows the calls came after the 09:03:09 cancellation.
The rider's own profile shows 3 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F16); the other side may cite this as a pattern, though NS-9 requires 3 *no-show cancellations* within 30 days, which is not shown.

The gap between the 3-minute mark and the cancellation is only ~1 second on the recorded times (F3: 2 min 59 s), so the other side may dispute the exact second of matching, although the timeline fact F3 is the system record.

claims.assertion: The rider, not the driver, cancelled the trip: the timeline records cancellation by rider at 09:03:09, 179 s after acceptance at 09:00:10, with the in-app reason 'rider_changed_plans' and the $5.00 fee on record.

This is an NS-4 rider-cancellation case, not an NS-1/NS-2 no-show case, so the $5.00 fee belongs to the driver under the official rule for cancellations later than 3 minutes after matching; the rider cancelled at 2 min 59 s, one second inside the free window's edge, so the fee stands.

The driver did in fact turn up at the pickup point: GPS places him first within 200 m at 09:02:40 with a closest approach of 39 m at 09:03:00, and the platform recorded arrival at 09:02:40, so the rider cannot claim the driver never arrived and NS-8 does not apply.

The rider's own complaint admits she 'gave up and cancelled' because she was held up upstairs, which is a rider-side cancellation for her own change of plan, not a driver failure; the written reason in the app (rider_changed_plans) matches that admission.

The driver made contact attempts and waited, and the two call logs at 09:06 and 09:07 show he tried to reach the rider even after the cancellation time; his account age of 1600 days, 4.9 rating, 700 trips in 90 days and zero disputes or upheld complaints show a long, clean record with no pattern of fee abuse.
No money beyond the fee is in issue: the fare record shows only the $5.00 cancellation fee with a 1.0x multiplier, so any order here concerns a single fixed $5.00 item.

weaknesses: NS-1's conditions are not met on this record and the other side will use that: before 09:03:09 the driver sent 0 in-app messages and made 0 in-app calls (F4), and there is no in-app chat at all (F9) — though the driver cannot be required to satisfy the no-show conditions because he did not cancel, this weakens any argument that the fee is separately justified by a completed no-show process.

The driver's written statement claims 'I waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice' (F12), but the system records show the rider cancelled 2 min 59 s after acceptance (F3), arrival at 09:02:40 and the calls at 09:06 and 09:07 (F10, F11) — i.e. after the trip was already cancelled. The other side will use F3 against F12 to attack the driver's credibility, and F12 is a statement that loses to the timeline.

Cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation is only 25 s (F2), so the driver cannot show any meaningful wait at the pickup point; his only real shield is that the rider cancelled first, at 09:03:09 (F3).

points.response: Conceded as far as the facts go: the cancellation was the rider's (F3). But the identity of the canceller only selects NS-4; it does not settle chargeability, which NS-4 makes turn on the 3-minute mark after matching.

Inverted: NS-4 charges only cancellations 'later than 3 minutes after matching', and the system record puts matching at 09:00:10 and cancellation at 09:03:09 — 2 min 59 s, i.e. inside the window — so the fee is not chargeable; being 'one second inside the edge' is still inside it.

Not contested that the driver arrived (F1, F2, F5) — NS-8 was never my ground; arrival alone establishes nothing, because NS-1 requires the 5-minute free wait (here 29 s from the 09:02:40 arrival to the 09:03:09 cancellation, F2/F5/F3), an in-app message and an in-app call before cancelling (F4 shows 0 and 0), all of which fail.

The rider's candour about being held up (F3) is exactly why NS-4 applies, and NS-4 does not ask why the rider changed plans inside the first 3 minutes — the reason field does not convert a free-window cancellation into a chargeable one.

The two calls at 09:06 and 09:07 (F10, F11) are after the 09:03:09 cancellation (F3), so they cannot be contact attempts 'before cancelling' and instead corroborate my reading of F12; a clean profile (F17) may bear on credibility but never decides the case.

This is the one point I genuinely cannot answer on the record: NS-4 makes a rider cancellation within 3 minutes of matching free, and F3 times the cancellation at 2 min 59 s, with no fact in the record showing any other chargeable ground (F4, F9, F10, F11 show no completed no-show process).
